target_customer: California HOA boards and homeowners in condo, townhome and single-family communities who pay management fees
problem: HOA management is reactive, confusing and inefficient; boards lack clarity and routine tasks are manual.

founders.name: Allen Liou
founders.background_notes: Real estate agent for several years, then customer success and implementation roles at unnamed startups, per YC page. Grew up in a townhome community.

founders.name: Shreyas Bharadwaj
founders.background_notes: Data scientist at startups and most recently at RAND, building experimental ML products for the DoD, per YC page. Joined an HOA board as a condo owner.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly workflow software and an LLM assistant (Atlas) on top of a services business; the hard part is operations and licensing of managers, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Management contracts with boards create some stickiness and local operating density, but the software is copyable and incumbents sell similar tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent HOA software vendors later marketed AI features (ALLi, HOAi per vendor pages from 2025 to 2026); no source shows any of them copying the management-company model.

market_need_then: Per YC page, founders experienced HOA inefficiencies firsthand as a board member and owner. The company reported 26 communities managed at launch and a 4.9 star Google rating (YC page).

branding.domain_note: Uses assemblyhoa.com (exact name plus HOA suffix); acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, trust-focused: mission is to build trust and transparency in communities

branding.brand_signature: Atlas, a free AI assistant for homeowners to understand governing documents

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself; the name is a common word shared with many companies, so search results mix it with unrelated Assembly firms. Atlas is a modest product hook.

outcome_analysis: Assembly remains active and, per its own site in 2026, claims 100+ California HOAs across 11 counties, up from 26 communities at its 2024 launch. Growth looks like steady services-led expansion with software as leverage and founder domain insight from HOA board and real estate experience. No funding was verified beyond aggregator figures, and no acquisition or failure news was found.
notes: Funding is unverified: aggregators disagree (about $1.8M seed Sept 2024 per VCBacked, $2M per Startup Intros, $330K seed in 2023 per another tracker, $2.3M total on a job listing). Reported investors from aggregators only: Y Combinator, General Catalyst, Bessemer, Pioneer Fund, TwentyTwo VC. None confirmed by a primary source, so no rounds are recorded. Competitor searches returned only 2025 to 2026 vendor pages, so the competitor list is empty. Education not stated on the YC page. Company site says founded 2022 per YC.
